own_scenes.desc: Fuera de Death Row, DJ Quik y MC Eiht, a menudo rivales, retrataron Compton: Quik, que aprendió sampleando «Computer Love» en la caja de ritmos que Kelvin Anderson compró a Sir Jinx, fue un productor de G-funk muy musical, «al nivel de Rakim» para los angelinos. Cypress Hill (Sen Dog, B-Real y DJ Muggs), de South Gate, unieron inglés y castellano, Compton y East L.A., y la marihuana sin complejos; su primer disco (Ruffhouse, 1991) tenía temática del Oeste y bases del Este, con «The Phuncky Feel One» / «How I Could Just Kill a Man».

refs.q: It was West Coast subject matter and vernacular, but the beats were East Coast.
refs.para: Chris Schwartz (cofounder, Ruffhouse): It was West Coast subject matter and vernacular, but the beats were East Coast. Back then, you could hear a West Coast record and East Coast record and know the difference immediately. But that’s what made it really cool.
